title: BRICS Tourism Ministers adopt Jaipur Declaration (Ministers’ Communique)
subtitle: “Tourism connects people; it creates opportunities for communities and enables cultural exchange”: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
body_text:
The BRICS Tourism Ministers ’ Meeting under India ’ s Chairship concluded in Jaipur today with the adoption of the BRICS Tourism Ministers ’ Communiqué 2026 (Jaipur Declaration), providing a framework for strengthening tourism cooperation among BRICS Member States.
The meeting was chaired by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. It marked the culmination of the BRICS Tourism Track under India ’ s Chairship in 2026, being taken forward under the theme “ Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
The meeting saw participation from nine BRICS Member States. Ministerial participation included Mr. Gustavo Costa Feliciando, Minister of Tourism, Brazil; Mr. Reza Salehi Amiri, Minister of Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts, Iran; Ms. Patricia De Lille, Minister of Tourism, South Africa; and H.E. Abdulla Bin Touq Al Marri, Minister of Economy and Tourism, United Arab Emirates, along with Heads of Delegation from China, Ethiopia, Indonesia and Russia. The Indian delegation included Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, and Shri Harikishore S., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, among other officials.
The Jaipur Declaration reflects the work undertaken through the BRICS Tourism Working Group during India ’ s Chairship around four thematic priorities — Artificial Intelligence and Tourism; Sustainability and Responsible Tourism; Tourism Skilling and Capacity Building; and Tourism Exchanges and Seamless Travel Facilitation.
The Ministers’ Communique adopted by consensus by BRICS Tourism Ministers recognises the transformative potential of responsible, safe and human-centred Artificial Intelligence and digital technologies in tourism and supports cooperation in tourism planning, destination management, visitor services, multilingual communication and travel facilitation.
It further places emphasis on sustainable and community-centred tourism, protection of natural and cultural heritage, tourism investment and infrastructure, development and promotion of diverse tourism products, continuous skilling and upskilling, industry-academia partnerships, exchange of tourism data and statistics, sharing of best practices and stronger people-to-people connectivity among BRICS Member States.
Addressing the meeting, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that tourism has an important role in India ’ s journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047 and has the unique ability to take growth beyond major economic centres to towns, villages and remote regions. He said tourism creates opportunities for hotels and homestays, taxi operators, guides, artisans, weavers, farmers, entrepreneurs and millions of families whose livelihoods are directly or indirectly connected with the sector.
The Minister highlighted India ’ s efforts to build a tourism ecosystem that is economically prosperous, environmentally responsible, technologically enabled and culturally authentic. He further remarked, “ Tourism ultimately connects people. It creates opportunities for communities, enables cultural exchange and allows citizens of our countries to understand one another beyond the formal relationships between governments.”
On the sidelines of the Tourism Ministers ’ Meeting, India held bilateral meetings with Brazil, Iran, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates. The engagements provided an opportunity for interaction with the respective Ministerial delegations and for taking forward tourism cooperation.
A press conference was also held on the BRICS Tourism Track under India ’ s Chairship, highlighting the outcomes of the Tourism Ministers ’ Meeting and the adoption of the Jaipur Declaration.
Alongside part of Tourism Ministerial Meeting in Jaipur, curated experiences spotlighting traditional arts, crafts and community-based tourism initiatives were showcased to Ministers and delegates.
On 22 August 2026, the Ministers and delegates will undertake a visit to some of Jaipur ’ s iconic heritage attractions, including Hawa Mahal, City Palace and Amber Fort, providing them an opportunity to experience the city ’ s rich architectural, cultural and tourism heritage.

enrichment.summary: The BRICS Tourism Ministers' Meeting, held under India's Chairship in Jaipur, concluded with the adoption of the BRICS Tourism Ministers' Communiqué 2026 (Jaipur Declaration). The declaration frames cooperation among BRICS states around four themes—AI in tourism, sustainability, skilling, and seamless travel facilitation—and was adopted by consensus by ministers from nine member states including Brazil, Iran, South Africa, UAE, China, Ethiopia, Indonesia and Russia. India also held bilateral meetings with several member states on the sidelines.
enrichment.context: BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, now expanded to include Iran, UAE, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia and others) rotates its annual chairship among members, with India holding it in 2026. Sectoral tracks like tourism, alongside finance, trade and health, form part of the broader BRICS cooperation architecture, culminating in ministerial declarations that set non-binding cooperative frameworks rather than binding agreements. The Jaipur Declaration fits into India's larger push to project tourism as a tool of soft power and economic diversification, tying into domestic initiatives like Dekho Apna Desh and the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, where tourism is positioned as a livelihood generator for informal-sector workers such as guides, homestay operators and artisans. Such communiqués are useful for aspirants mainly as markers of India's evolving role in multilateral groupings and its diplomatic calendar, rather than as substantive policy shifts, since they largely reaffirm cooperative intent on themes like AI-enabled tourism and sustainable/responsible tourism without binding commitments or budgetary allocations.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Jaipur Declaration' of 2026 was adopted at a ministerial meeting held under which grouping's chairship?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Jaipur Declaration was adopted at the BRICS Tourism Ministers' Meeting held under India's Chairship of BRICS in 2026.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following was NOT listed as one of the four thematic priorities of the BRICS Tourism Working Group under India's Chairship in 2026?
prelims_questions.explanation: The four thematic priorities were AI and Tourism, Sustainability and Responsible Tourism, Tourism Skilling and Capacity Building, and Tourism Exchanges and Seamless Travel Facilitation; taxation harmonization was not among them.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of sectoral cooperation tracks, such as tourism, within multilateral groupings like BRICS for India's foreign policy and economic diplomacy.
Examine the potential of tourism as an instrument for inclusive economic growth and livelihood generation in India, especially in non-metropolitan and remote regions.

study_notes.reason: The release is essentially a diplomatic communique with factual details (venue, chairship, thematic priorities, member states) that could support objective questions, while offering little genuine analytical depth beyond generic soft-power framing already covered in context.

prelims.point: India held the BRICS Tourism Track Chairship in 2026, culminating in the Jaipur Declaration/BRICS Tourism Ministers' Communiqué 2026
prelims.why_important: Chairship rotation and host country of sectoral BRICS meetings is a common factual detail UPSC tests to gauge awareness of India's multilateral diplomatic calendar.

prelims.point: The Jaipur Declaration's four thematic priorities: AI and Tourism, Sustainability and Responsible Tourism, Tourism Skilling and Capacity Building, and Seamless Travel Facilitation
prelims.why_important: UPSC could frame a match-the-following or 'which of these are themes of X declaration' question from such thematic lists.

prelims.point: Nine BRICS member states participated, including newer entrants Iran, UAE, Ethiopia and Indonesia alongside founding members Brazil, Russia, China, South Africa
prelims.why_important: Knowing the expanded BRICS membership list is a recurring prelims requirement given the 2024 expansion.

prelims.point: BRICS meetings such as this one adopt Communiqués/Declarations by consensus, which are non-binding cooperative frameworks rather than treaties
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing non-binding declarations from binding international agreements is a classic conceptual distinction UPSC likes to test.

mains.point: India is using sectoral tracks like tourism within BRICS to project soft power and diversify its economic and diplomatic engagement beyond core groupings like G20 or SCO
mains.analytical_use: Useful for a question on how India leverages multilateral platforms for non-traditional sectors to advance foreign policy goals.

mains.point: Tourism is positioned domestically as a livelihood generator for informal-sector workers (guides, homestay operators, artisans) linked to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision
mains.analytical_use: Can support an answer on tourism's role in generating employment and regional economic dispersal beyond metro cities.
